q: Why does fixed-size chunking often hurt retrieval?
options: It cuts through sentences, tables and sections, producing chunks that make no sense alone
explain: Boundaries that ignore structure create orphaned fragments that match poorly.

q: What does contextual retrieval add to each chunk before indexing?
options: A short generated note situating the chunk in its document
A summary of the whole corpus
explain: The note resolves references like “it” and adds the document and section context.

q: In small-to-big retrieval, what is returned to the model?
options: The larger parent section of the matched chunk
explain: Small chunks match precisely; their parents give the model enough context.
